_doc: Enforcement manifest template: one object per floor rule, binding it to its honest enforcement point. Prose and rationale: docs/enforcement-manifest.md. Fill the angle-bracket placeholders, replace the example rules with your floor, and pair the file with a CI coverage gate that fails when a rule loses its mechanical check, flips to review without a reason, or drops its non_delegable flag.
_contract: enforcement is honest, not aspirational: lint = universal static guard that sees whole files; test = dedicated test file; harness = behavioral coverage through the real path on representative routes; review = no viable low-false-positive static check exists, and reason names the compensating control. Rules marked non_delegable are NEVER approved by an LLM verify in place of the mechanical check; a model pass may run in addition to the gate, never instead of it.

rules.rule: All queries are parameterized. Never an f-string with user input.
rules.reason: No low-false-positive static check exists: interpolating trusted constants into query strings is idiomatic and indistinguishable from user-input interpolation without taint analysis, so a naive grep would drown real hits in false positives. Compensating controls: the in-process test harness records every query configuration so parameter usage is observable in tests, and this zone carries a higher human-audit rate than mechanically gated zones.

rules.rule: No new inline <style> or <script> blocks in the page shell; CSS and JS live in their own files.
Every endpoint that touches user data resolves the caller through the one shared auth helper first.
rules.reason: Anonymous requests get 401/403 and role-gated routes are exercised through the real auth path in the in-process harness, on representative routes. A universal static sweep over every route is deferred until an accurate public-route allowlist exists; the manifest states that honestly rather than claiming lint coverage that is not there.

rules.rule: Migrations are forward-only. Never roll back schema; add new columns instead, and old columns stay with a deprecation note.
